# WORK BREAKDOWN STRUCTURE
## Underground CBRN-hardened blast-resistant protective structure and sentry post — Pune, Maharashtra

**Works Management package revision WM1** · 07 September 2026
**Geometry:** Architectural Rev F · Structural Phase 2 Rev A + M1 · **Services:** Drainage DR1 · HVAC HV1 · Schedule of Finishes FN1 · Structural CAD SC1
**Evidence classes:** `[C]` confirmed · `[D]` derived here · `[A]` assumed by this package ·
`[U]` unresolved · `[N]` not available — data required

> **THE ONLY DESIGN CHANGE in this package is reference SP-B1: the sentry post walls
> are BRICK MASONRY, replacing the Rev F 200 mm RC ballistic infill panels.
> No other element of the project is changed.**

---

The WBS covers the complete project from mobilisation to handover: the main
underground shelter, the entry structures, the sentry post, all services, the
external works and the concealment works. It has three levels — fourteen level-1
work packages, sixty level-2 sub-packages and 279 level-3 activities of which
eighteen are milestones.

The WBS and the programme are the same data. Every activity code below appears in
`Underground_Shelter_Final_Works_Programme.xml` with the same identifier, the same
duration and the same logic, and every BOQ item is measured against one of these
work packages.

|---|---|

| Level-2 sub-packages | 60 |
| Level-3 activities | 279 (of which 18 milestones) |
| Logic links | 404 |
| Duration | 326 working days, 02 Nov 2026 to 20 Nov 2027 |

## WBS coding rules

1. **Level 1** is a work package that could be let as a separate sub-contract or
   reported on separately to the client.
2. **Level 2** groups activities that share a work face, a trade and a set of hold
   points.
3. **Level 3** is an activity that one gang can be instructed to do, that has a
   measurable quantity behind it, and that can be marked complete without
   ambiguity.
4. Milestones carry zero duration and no resource. They are reporting events, not
   work.
5. Hold points are activities in their own right (they consume time and require
   the Engineer's attendance) and are named `HOLD POINT:` so that they cannot be
   passed over silently.
6. Activity numbering follows the level-1 package: `A1xxx` pre-construction,
   `A2xxx` earthworks, `A3xxx` substructure, `A4xxx` pressure slab, `A5xxx` entry
   structures, `A6xxx` waterproofing, `A7xxx` cover, `A8xxx` sentry post, `A9xxx`
   mechanical and CBRN, `A10xxx` drainage, `A11xxx` electrical and EMP, `A12xxx`
   finishes, `A13xxx` external works, `A14xxx` testing and handover.

## Where this WBS departs from the supplied R0 schedule

The supplied `UG CBRN HDRND OPS ROOM MCS — R0` schedule was used as the starting
point and its project start date, six-day calendar and the practice of naming the
structural consultant's checks as separate activities have all been kept. The
structure itself was rebuilt, because the R0 schedule describes a different
building:

| R0 activity | Why it is not in this WBS |
|---|---|

| Lift / lift shaft | The supplied R0 schedule contains 'Column, Staircase & Lift Shear Wall' activities. THERE IS NO LIFT ANYWHERE IN THIS PROJECT. Those activities are generic building boilerplate and have been removed. |
| Second grade slab over 4 m of overburden | The R0 schedule programmes a '2nd Slab (Ground Lvl) Grade Slab' over '4m Soil Overburdon'. The current design has a SINGLE 900 pressure slab at (-)2.000 under 2000 of layered engineered cover containing a 200 M30 burster slab. The 4 m arrangement is a superseded revision. |
| 1000 mm roof slab | The R0 schedule calls the roof '1st Slab (1000 mm Thk)'. The confirmed thickness is 900. |
| Structural RC columns in the shelter | None exists. The box is a wall-and-slab structure; master B.3 declares punching shear NOT APPLICABLE for the same reason, and Structural CAD SC1 records that drawing a column sheet would be fabrication. |
| Dado / wall tiling in the shelter | The R0 schedule programmes wall tiles. The Schedule of Finishes states the opposite for the gas-tight envelope: 'NO joints, NO tiles, NO grout — grout lines are a decontamination failure'. Tiling is therefore not programmed inside the envelope. |
| Suspended ceilings and gypsum punning in the shelter | The R0 schedule programmes gypsum punning to ceilings. FN1 forbids any suspended ceiling or boxing-in in the gas-tight envelope for three confirmed reasons: duct inspectability, pipe inspectability and contamination trapping. |

The R0 schedule also contained no sentry post as an identifiable structure, no
escape shafts, no blast doors, no CBRN plant, no EMP works, no engineered cover
build-up, no burster slab, no camouflage or concealment works, no procurement
activities, no commissioning sequence and one milestone. All of those are project
scope and all of them are now in the WBS.
